name: Earthy Black Girl
summary: Unlike the Hippie and Boho-Chic aesthetics, for which it is often confused, Earthy Black Girl does not appropriate West African cultural traditions; instead, it uses them with curiosity and respect to reconnect Black Americans with cultures institutionally removed from them through Slavery.
description:
Unlike the Hippie and Boho-Chic aesthetics, for which it is often confused, Earthy Black Girl does not appropriate West African cultural traditions; instead, it uses them with curiosity and respect to reconnect Black Americans with cultures institutionally removed from them through Slavery. Hippie and Bohemian styles also more heavily take inspiration from the Roma people of Europe, [ 1 ] another oppressed minority, though modern Boho-Chic specifically does take inspiration from African fashion as well.

It is related to Ethnochic , new age spirituality and mysticism, and more recently, to the Black Nouveau interior design movement.

The closest aesthetic that is not tied to the Black identity is Boho-Chic . Many south Asian women, particularly Indian women, resonate with this aesthetic due to similar looks and shared spiritual beliefs. [ 1 ]
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Cultural and ancestral pride, mysticism, spirituality, connection with the Earth, Black identity, femininity and the divine feminine

visualDNA.colour: Orange, green, brown, yellow, red, black and white

fashion.Overview: As this is an aesthetic made by and for women, the fashion for it is hyperfeminine. Since it is Afrocentric, it relies heavily on both Black American and African popular cultures. For example, you will see lots of beading and shells, but rarely any bows or ribbons despite being hyperfeminine -- this is due to the cultural differences between Black and white Americans. Africa is hot and humid (Central West Africa) or hot and dry (North/South Africa), so the garments here are light and airy, and show a decent amount of skin -- African cultures do not believe that showing your arms, midriff, back or legs are inappropriate like many other cultures do, and so the clothing is less conservative…
fashion.Tops: Tank tops, camisoles, and bandeau tops; Loose, knit or crochet cardigans, often cropped; Crop tops; Tie-front tops and blouses; Off-the-shoulder tops; Flared sleeves, bell sleeves, angel sleeves
fashion.Bottoms: Long, flowing midi and maxi skirts; Patchwork and tiered skirts; Cargo mini shorts; Cargo pants; Flared denim jeans
fashion.Dresses: Rompers, jumpsuits and playsuits, particularly loose-fitted and non-restrictive ones
fashion.Shoes: Sandals, flip-flops, and slides; Clogs; Go-go boots; Barefoot
fashion.Accessories: Headwraps, head scarves, bandanas and headbands; Hoop and dangly gold and jade earrings; Large golden bangles; Beaded bracelets, sometimes with cowrie, puka, or other types of shells; Chain belts, shield belts; Waist beads; Arm cuffs; Hair/braid cuffs, braid charms, coils and hair rings; Tattoos and henna
fashion.Hair, Makeup and Beauty: Dark, earthy, and warm toned makeup; Shea butter, cocoa butter (lotions, balms, oils); Scents like vanilla, Egyptian musk, patchouli, brown sugar, and cocoa butter
